docs.title: spectracles
docs.text: Spectrospatial modelling with JAX and Equinox.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install spectracles

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import spectracles as sp

# Build a model
model = sp.build_model(MyModel, ...)

# Create an optimization schedule
schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[(100, 0.1), (50, 0.01)],
    params={
        "*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1),
        "*.kernel.*": sp.free_after(1),
    },
)

# Run optimization
schedule.run_all(x=data_x, y=data_y)

docs.title: Schedule Builder API
docs.text: A declarative, parameter-centric API for building optimization schedules with minimal boilerplate.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from spectracles import build_schedule, free_in, free_after, init_normal
import jax.random as jr

schedule = build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (100, 0.1),   # 100 steps, lr=0.1
        (50, 0.01),   # 50 steps, lr=0.01
    ],
    params={
        "gp.coefficients": free_in(0, 1),
        "gp.kernel.*": free_after(1),
        "line.amplitude": free_in(1) | init_normal(0, std=0.1),
    },
    key=jr.key(42),
)

schedule.run_all(x=data_x, y=data_y)

docs.title: free_in(*phases)
docs.text:
Parameter is free (optimized) only in the specified phases.

"param": free_in(0, 2, 4)  # Free in phases 0, 2, and 4

docs.title: free_after(phase)
docs.text:
Parameter is free from the specified phase onwards.

"param": free_after(1)  # Fixed in phase 0, free in phases 1, 2, 3, ...

docs.title: free_until(phase)
docs.text:
Parameter is free up to and including the specified phase.

"param": free_until(1)  # Free in phases 0 and 1, fixed afterwards

docs.title: fixed_in(*phases)
docs.text:
Parameter is fixed only in the specified phases, free elsewhere.

"param": fixed_in(0)  # Fixed in phase 0, free in all other phases

docs.title: Initialization Helpers
docs.text: Initialize parameters at the start of a phase.

docs.title: init_value(phase, value)
docs.text:
Set parameter to a specific value.

"param": free_after(1) | init_value(1, 2.5)  # Set to 2.5 at start of phase 1

docs.title: init_normal(phase, mean=0.0, std=1.0)
docs.text:
Initialize with random normal values. Requires passing key to build_schedule.

"param": free_in(0) | init_normal(0, mean=0.0, std=0.1)

docs.title: init_uniform(phase, low=0.0, high=1.0)
docs.text:
Initialize with random uniform values. Requires passing key to build_schedule.

"param": free_in(0) | init_uniform(0, low=-1.0, high=1.0)

docs.title: Combining Specs
docs.text:
Use | to combine free/fixed specs with initialization:

"param": free_in(0, 1, 2) | init_normal(0) | init_value(2, 1.0)

docs.title: Pattern Matching
docs.text:
Glob-style patterns match parameter paths:

Pattern Matches "param" Exact match "inner.param" Exact nested match "*.param" inner1.param, inner2.param, etc. "gp.kernel.*" All attributes of gp.kernel "gp.*.lengthscale" gp.kernel.lengthscale, gp.mean.lengthscale, etc. "**.lengthscale" Any lengthscale at any depth

docs.title: Phase Specification
docs.text:
Phases are tuples of (n_steps, learning_rate) or (n_steps, learning_rate, optimizer):

phases=[
    (100, 0.1),                    # Uses default optimizer (adam)
    (50, 0.01),
    (50, 0.001, optax.sgd(0.001)), # Custom optimizer
]

docs.title: Full API
docs.text:
schedule = build_schedule(
    model,                          # ShareModule to optimize
    loss_fn,                        # Loss function
    phases,                         # List of phase specs
    params,                         # Dict of pattern -> ParamSpec
    default_optimizer="adam",       # "adam" or "sgd"
    managed=False,                  # Return ManagedOptimiserSchedule if True
    get_filter_spec_fn=get_opt_filter_spec,  # Selects which leaves are optimised
    Δloss_criterion=None,           # Early-stopping threshold (None = off)
    key=None,                       # PRNG key for random initialization
)

docs.title: Early Stopping
docs.text:
Pass Δloss_criterion to let phases exit before their full n_steps. From step 100 onwards, every 50 steps, a phase stops if the loss changed by less than Δloss_criterion over the previous 50 steps:

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[(5000, 0.1), (5000, 0.01)],
    params={"**": sp.free_in(0, 1)},
    Δloss_criterion=1e-2,
)

The same threshold applies to every phase. build_schedule defaults to None (no early stopping). A PhaseConfig constructed directly defaults to 1e2.

docs.title: Shared Parameters
docs.text:
When parameters are shared, only specify the parent path (not the shared copies). The builder validates this and will error if you try to specify a shared path directly.

# If 'b' is shared from 'a':
params={
    "a": free_in(0),  # Correct - use parent path
    # "b": free_in(0),  # Error - 'b' is a shared path
}

docs.title: Example: Multi-Phase Optimization
docs.text:
schedule = build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (200, 0.1),    # Phase 0: Warm up coefficients
        (100, 0.05),   # Phase 1: Refine with kernel
        (50, 0.01),    # Phase 2: Fine tune everything
    ],
    params={
        # Coefficients: always free
        "*.coefficients": free_in(0, 1, 2),

        # Kernel params: free after warm-up
        "*.kernel.*": free_after(1),

        # Amplitude: reinitialize at phase 1
        "line.amplitude": free_after(1) | init_normal(1, std=0.5),
    },
    key=jr.key(0),
)

schedule.run_all(x=x, y=y)
final_model = schedule.model_history[-1]

docs.title: spectracles.model.kernels.LogLogLinear
docs.text:
Bases: Kernel

Log-log-linear CFM kernel: log-amplitude PSD is linear in log(k).

feature_weights(freqs) = exp(m_0 + m_s * log(k)) with DC (k=0) forced to zero so the fluctuation field has zero mean by construction. The field's spatial mean should be provided separately via FourierGP.zeromode.

m_s is the spectral index; m_0 the log-amplitude. For negative m_s (the physically common regime) the continuous PSD is IR-divergent, which is why the DC term must be handled as a separate Parameter outside the PSD.

docs.title: spectracles.optimise.opt_schedule.OptimiserSchedule
docs.text:
Multi-phase optimization schedule for ShareModule models.

Runs a sequence of optimization phases, each with its own optimizer, learning rate, and parameter configuration. Tracks model history across phases.

Attributes:

Name Type Description phases

List of Phase objects defining the schedule.

model_history

List of models, one for initial state plus one after each completed phase.

Examples:

>>> schedule = OptimiserSchedule(
...     model, loss_fn,
...     phase_configs=[
...         PhaseConfig(n_steps=100, optimiser=optax.adam(0.1)),
...         PhaseConfig(n_steps=50, optimiser=optax.adam(0.01)),
...     ],
... )
>>> schedule.run_all(x=data_x, y=data_y)
>>> final_model = schedule.model_history[-1]
See Also

ManagedOptimiserSchedule: Version with state tracking, skip, and reset. build_schedule: Declarative API for building schedules.

docs.title: spectracles.optimise.opt_schedule.ManagedOptimiserSchedule
docs.text:
Multi-phase optimization schedule with state tracking and control.

Extends OptimiserSchedule with phase state management, allowing you to: - Run phases one at a time with run_next_phase() - Skip phases with skip_phase() - Reset and re-run with reset() or reset_from_phase() - Inspect progress with get_phase_status(), is_complete(), etc.

Phases must be run in order. The schedule tracks which phases are pending, running, completed, or skipped.

Attributes:

Name Type Description phases

List of Phase objects defining the schedule.

model_history

List of models, one for initial state plus one after each completed phase.

phase_states

List of PhaseState values tracking each phase's status.

current_phase_index

Index of the next phase to run.

initial_model

The original model (kept for reset functionality).

Examples:

>>> schedule = ManagedOptimiserSchedule(model, loss_fn, phase_configs)
>>>
>>> # Run phases one at a time
>>> schedule.run_next_phase(x=x, y=y)
>>> print(f"Phase 0 loss: {schedule.loss_history[-1]:.4f}")
>>>
>>> # Check status
>>> print(schedule.get_phase_status())
{'current_phase': 1, 'total_phases': 3, 'completed_phases': 1, ...}
>>>
>>> # Skip a phase if needed
>>> schedule.skip_phase(1)
>>>
>>> # Run remaining phases
>>> schedule.run_all(x=x, y=y)
>>>
>>> # Reset and try again
>>> schedule.reset()
>>> schedule.run_all(x=x, y=y)
See Also

OptimiserSchedule: Simpler version without state tracking. build_schedule: Declarative API with managed=True option.

docs.title: spectracles.optimise.opt_schedule.PhaseConfig dataclass
docs.text:
Configuration for a single optimization phase.

Defines the number of steps, optimizer, and any parameter updates to apply at the start of the phase.

Attributes:

Name Type Description n_steps int

Number of optimization steps to run in this phase.

optimiser GradientTransformation

An optax optimizer (e.g., optax.adam(0.01)).

Δloss_criterion float | None

Early-stopping threshold on the loss change over 50 steps (default 1e2). None disables early stopping.

fix_status_updates dict[str, bool]

Dict mapping parameter paths to their fixed status. True means fixed (not optimized), False means free.

param_val_updates dict[str, Array]

Dict mapping parameter paths to new values to set at the start of this phase.

Examples:

>>> config = PhaseConfig(
...     n_steps=100,
...     optimiser=optax.adam(0.01),
...     fix_status_updates={"gp.kernel.lengthscale": True},
...     param_val_updates={"gp.coefficients": jnp.zeros(10)},
... )

docs.title: spectracles.optimise.schedule_builder.build_schedule(model, loss_fn, phases, params, default_optimizer='adam', managed=False, get_filter_spec_fn=get_opt_filter_spec, Δloss_criterion=None, key=None)
docs.text:
Build an optimization schedule using a parameter-centric specification.

This function provides a declarative way to specify which parameters should be free or fixed in each phase, with automatic pattern expansion for parameter paths.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default model ShareModule

The ShareModule to optimize.

required loss_fn Callable[..., float]

Loss function to minimize.

required phases list[Union[PhaseSpec, PhaseSpecFull]]

List of phase specifications. Each is either: - (n_steps, learning_rate): Uses default optimizer - (n_steps, learning_rate, optimizer): Uses specified optimizer

required params dict[str, ParamSpec]

Dictionary mapping parameter patterns to ParamSpecs. Patterns support glob-style matching: - "*" matches any single component - "**" matches any number of components

required default_optimizer Literal['sgd', 'adam']

Default optimizer type ("sgd" or "adam").

'adam' managed bool

If True, return a ManagedOptimiserSchedule with state tracking.

False get_filter_spec_fn Callable[[ShareModule], Callable]

Function to get filter spec for optimization.

get_opt_filter_spec Δloss_criterion Optional[float]

Early-stopping threshold applied to every phase. From step 100, every 50 steps, a phase exits early if the loss changed by less than this over the last 50 steps. None (default) disables early stopping.

None key Optional[PRNGKeyArray]

PRNG key for random initializations. Required if any init_normal or init_uniform specs are used.

None

Returns:

Type Description Union[OptimiserSchedule, ManagedOptimiserSchedule]

An OptimiserSchedule or ManagedOptimiserSchedule ready to run.

Examples:

>>> schedule = build_schedule(
...     model, loss_fn,
...     phases=[
...         (100, 0.1),    # Phase 0: 100 steps, lr=0.1
...         (50, 0.01),    # Phase 1: 50 steps, lr=0.01
...         (50, 0.001),   # Phase 2: 50 steps, lr=0.001
...     ],
...     params={
...         "gp.coefficients": free_in(0, 1, 2),
...         "gp.kernel.*": free_after(1),
...         "line.amplitude": free_in(1, 2) | init_normal(0),
...     },
... )
>>> schedule.run_all(data)

docs.title: ShareModule
docs.text: ShareModule is a wrapper around JAX/Equinox models that enables parameter sharing and provides utilities for model inspection and manipulation.

docs.title: Building Models
docs.text:
Use build_model() to construct your Equinox model and wrap it in a ShareModule. Pass the model class followed by its constructor arguments:

import spectracles as sp

# Equivalent to wrapping MyModel(shared_component=inner, ...)
model = sp.build_model(MyModel, shared_component=inner, ...)

docs.title: Parameter Paths
docs.text:
# Get all unique parameter paths (excludes shared duplicates and Known)
paths = model.get_parameter_paths()

# Include shared parameters
paths = model.get_parameter_paths(show_shared=True)

# Include Known parameters
paths = model.get_parameter_paths(show_knowns=True)

docs.title: Parameter Summary
docs.text:
# Print a rich table of all parameters
model.get_parameter_summary()

Shows path, shape, bounds, free/fixed status, and sharing info for each parameter.

docs.title: Sharing Summary
docs.text:
# Component-level: which modules are the same object
model.get_sharing_summary(level="component")
# Returns: {'line_1.v': ['line_2.v']}

# Parameter-level: which parameter values are shared
model.get_sharing_summary(level="parameter")
# Returns: {'line_1.v.coefficients': ['line_2.v.coefficients']}

docs.title: Model Tree
docs.text:
# Print the model structure
model.print_model_tree()

# Include sharing relationships
model.print_model_tree(show_sharing=True)

docs.title: Model Graph
docs.text:
# Plot the model as a directed graph
model.plot_model_graph()

# Component-level view (shared modules point to same node)
model.plot_model_graph(sharing_level="component")

# Parameter-level view (shows all paths)
model.plot_model_graph(sharing_level="parameter")

docs.title: Setting Values
docs.text:
# Set a single parameter
model = model.set("line_1.A.coefficients", new_value)

# Set multiple parameters
model = model.set(
    ["path.to.param1", "path.to.param2"],
    [value1, value2]
)

docs.title: Fixing/Freeing Parameters
docs.text:
# Fix parameters (won't be optimized)
model = model.set_fixed_status(["path.to.param"], [True])

# Free parameters
model = model.set_fixed_status(["path.to.param"], [False])

# Fix all parameters
model = model.fix_all()

# Free all parameters
model = model.free_all()

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
# Check sharing structure is valid
info = model.validate_sharing()

docs.title: get_parameter_paths(show_shared=False, show_knowns=False)
docs.text:
Get all parameter paths that can be used with the set() method.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default show_shared bool

If False (default), only returns paths to unique/parent parameters. If True, also includes paths to shared (duplicate) parameters.

False show_knowns bool

If False (default), excludes Known parameters from the results. Known parameters are fixed constants that cannot be optimized.

False

Returns:

Type Description list[str]

A list of parameter path strings (e.g., ['line.A.coefficients',

list[str]

'line.v.coefficients']).

Examples:

>>> model.get_parameter_paths()
['line_1.A.coefficients', 'line_1.v.coefficients', 'line_2.A.coefficients']
>>> model.get_parameter_paths(show_shared=True)
['line_1.A.coefficients', 'line_1.v.coefficients', 'line_2.A.coefficients',
 'line_2.v.coefficients']  # line_2.v is shared with line_1.v

docs.title: get_parameter_summary(show_shared=True, show_knowns=False)
docs.text:
Print a summary table of all parameters with their status.

Shows path, shape, bounds, free/fixed status, and sharing info.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default show_shared bool

If True (default), include parameters that are shared from other parameters. If False, only show unique/parent parameters.

True show_knowns bool

If False (default), exclude Known parameters from the summary. If True, include them with status 'known'.

False

Examples:

>>> model.get_parameter_summary()
Parameter Summary
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Path                      Shape     Bounds       Status  Shared from
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
line_1.A.coefficients     (10,)     (-∞, ∞)      free    -
line_1.v.coefficients     (10,)     (-∞, ∞)      fixed   -
line_2.v.coefficients     (10,)     (-∞, ∞)      fixed   line_1.v.coefficients
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3 parameters (2 unique, 1 shared) · 1 free, 2 fixed

docs.title: get_sharing_summary(level='component')
docs.text:
Get a summary of what is shared in the model.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default level str

What level of sharing to report: - 'component': Shows which modules are the same object. (e.g., 'line_1.v' -> ['line_2.v']) - 'parameter': Shows which leaf parameter arrays are shared. More comprehensive, catches sharing done via tree_at. (e.g., 'line_1.v' -> ['line_2.v'])

'component'

Returns:

Type Description dict[str, list[str]]

A dictionary mapping parent paths to lists of paths that share

dict[str, list[str]]

with them. Only items that are actually shared are included.

Examples:

>>> model.get_sharing_summary()
{'line_1.v': ['line_2.v']}

docs.title: print_model_tree(show_sharing=False)
docs.text:
Print the model tree in an easy to parse format.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default show_sharing bool

If True, also print summaries of sharing relationships after the tree. Shows both shared modules (entire modules that are the same object) and shared parameters. Default is False for backwards compatibility.

False

Example with show_sharing=True: └── model (LineRatioModel) ├── line_1 (EmissionLine) │ └── v (GPField) └── line_2 (LinkedEmissionLine) └── v (GPField)

Shared modules (parameters within are also shared):
  line_1.v:
    ← line_2.v

Shared parameters:
  line_1.v.coefficients:
    ← line_2.v.coefficients

docs.title: plot_model_graph(ax=None, show=True, label_func=None, nx_draw_kwds=DEFAULT_NX_KWDS, sharing_level='component')
docs.text:
Plot the model as a graph using networkx and matplotlib. The graph is directed towards parameters and accounts for the sharing structure.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ax Axes | None

Matplotlib axes to plot on. If None, creates a new figure.

None show bool

If True, calls plt.show() after plotting.

True label_func Callable[[DiGraph], Dict[int, str]] | None

Custom function to generate node labels.

None nx_draw_kwds dict

Keyword arguments for networkx drawing functions.

DEFAULT_NX_KWDS sharing_level str

How to display sharing - 'component' (default) shows module-level sharing, 'parameter' shows leaf-level sharing.

'component'

docs.title: set(params, values, allow_set_knowns=False)
docs.text:
Return a new model with updated parameter values. Can only be used to update values of Parameters or ConstrainedParameters. The model must not be locked.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default params list[str]

List of parameter paths to update.

required values list[Array]

List of new values for each parameter.

required allow_set_knowns bool

If False (default), raises an error when trying to set Known parameters. Set to True to allow modifying Known values (use with caution).

False

Returns:

Type Description Self

A new ShareModule with updated parameter values.

docs.title: set_fixed_status(params, fix)
docs.text:
Return a new model with parameters updated to be fixed or not based on provided paths and list of bools. Can only be used to update fixed statuses of Parameters or ConstrainedParameters. The model must not be locked.

Known parameters cannot be unfixed - they are always fixed by definition.

docs.title: fix_all()
docs.text:
Return a new model with all parameters set to fixed.

This is useful for freezing all parameters, e.g., when you want to use the model for inference only without any further optimization.

Returns:

Type Description Self

A new ShareModule with all parameters fixed.

Examples:

>>> model = build_model(MyModel, ...)
>>> frozen_model = model.fix_all()
>>> # All parameters are now fixed

docs.title: free_all()
docs.text:
Return a new model with all parameters set to free (not fixed).

This is useful for unfreezing all parameters for optimization.

Returns:

Type Description Self

A new ShareModule with all parameters free.

Examples:

>>> frozen_model = model.fix_all()
>>> unfrozen_model = frozen_model.free_all()
>>> # All parameters are now free

docs.title: validate_sharing(raise_on_error=True)
docs.text:
Validate the sharing structure of the model.

Checks that: 1. All Shared objects reference valid parent parameters 2. Parent parameters exist and have the expected shape 3. No orphaned Shared objects exist

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default raise_on_error bool

If True (default), raises ValueError on validation failure. If False, returns validation results without raising.

True

Returns:

Type Description dict[str, Any]

A dictionary containing validation results:

dict[str, Any]
  • 'valid': bool - True if all checks passed
dict[str, Any]
  • 'n_shared_params': int - Number of shared parameter relationships
dict[str, Any]
  • 'n_unique_params': int - Number of unique parameters
dict[str, Any]
  • 'errors': list[str] - List of error messages (empty if valid)

Examples:

>>> result = model.validate_sharing(raise_on_error=False)
>>> if not result['valid']:
...     print("Errors:", result['errors'])

docs.title: copy()
docs.text: Create a proper copy of the ShareModule with correct sharing structure preserved and duplicated array data. It's like deepcopy but preserves the sharing structure.

docs.title: get_locked_model()
docs.text: Get a locked model. Locked models do not properly track shared parameters and so can no longer be optimised. Since all model parameters contained their actual values instead of some containing Shared objects, any subcomponent of the model may be called to make predictions, which is the primary use case for a locked model. You can't convert a locked model back, but this function returns a copy anyway so it doesn't matter.

docs.title: debug_repr()
docs.text: Return the full equinox-style repr for debugging.

docs.title: Schedule Builder Examples
docs.text: Practical examples of using the schedule builder API.

docs.title: Basic: Single Parameter
docs.text:
Optimize a simple model with one parameter:

import spectracles as sp
import jax.numpy as jnp

# Build model
model = sp.build_model(MyModel, value=1.0)

# Loss function
def loss_fn(model, x, y):
    return jnp.mean((model(x) - y) ** 2)

# Single phase, single parameter
schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[(100, 0.1)],
    params={
        "param": sp.free_in(0),
    },
)

schedule.run_all(x=x_data, y=y_data)
final_model = schedule.model_history[-1]

docs.title: Staged Optimization
docs.text:
Common pattern: warm up some parameters first, then refine others.

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (200, 0.1),   # Phase 0: High LR warm-up
        (100, 0.01),  # Phase 1: Lower LR refinement
        (50, 0.001),  # Phase 2: Fine-tuning
    ],
    params={
        # Coefficients: optimize throughout
        "*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),

        # Kernel parameters: freeze during warm-up
        "*.kernel.lengthscale": sp.free_after(1),
        "*.kernel.variance": sp.free_after(1),

        # Noise: only fine-tune at the end
        "noise": sp.free_in(2),
    },
)

docs.title: Reinitializing Parameters
docs.text:
Sometimes you want to reset a parameter partway through:

import jax.random as jr

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (100, 0.1),  # Phase 0
        (100, 0.1),  # Phase 1: restart amplitude
        (50, 0.01),  # Phase 2
    ],
    params={
        "gp.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),

        # Reset amplitude to random values at phase 1
        "line.amplitude": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2) | sp.init_normal(1, mean=0.0, std=0.5),

        # Set width to specific value at phase 1
        "line.width": sp.free_after(1) | sp.init_value(1, 1.0),
    },
    key=jr.key(42),  # Required for init_normal
)

docs.title: Wildcard Patterns
docs.text:
Match multiple parameters with glob patterns:

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[(100, 0.1), (50, 0.01)],
    params={
        # All coefficients in any submodule
        "*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1),

        # All kernel parameters (lengthscale, variance, etc.)
        "*.kernel.*": sp.free_after(1),

        # Any parameter named 'noise' at any depth
        "**.noise": sp.free_in(1),
    },
)

docs.title: Pattern Reference
docs.text: Pattern Matches "param" Exact match "gp.kernel.lengthscale" Exact nested path "*.param" inner1.param, inner2.param "gp.*" gp.coefficients, gp.kernel, etc. "gp.*.lengthscale" gp.kernel.lengthscale, gp.spatial.lengthscale "**.lengthscale" Any lengthscale at any depth

docs.title: Using Different Optimizers
docs.text:
Override the default optimizer per-phase:

import optax

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (100, 0.1),                      # Uses default (adam)
        (50, 0.01, optax.sgd(0.01)),     # Explicit SGD
        (50, 0.001, optax.adamw(0.001)), # AdamW with weight decay
    ],
    params={
        "*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),
    },
    default_optimizer="adam",  # Default for phases without explicit optimizer
)

docs.title: Managed Schedule (Interactive)
docs.text:
Use ManagedOptimiserSchedule for more control:

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (100, 0.1),
        (50, 0.01),
        (50, 0.001),
    ],
    params={
        "*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),
        "*.kernel.*": sp.free_after(1),
    },
    managed=True,  # Returns ManagedOptimiserSchedule
)

# Run phases one at a time
schedule.run_next_phase(x=x_data, y=y_data)
print(f"Phase 0 done, loss: {schedule.loss_history[-1]:.4f}")

# Check status
print(schedule.get_phase_status())

# Skip a phase if needed
schedule.skip_phase(1)

# Run remaining
schedule.run_all(x=x_data, y=y_data)

# Reset and try again with different data
schedule.reset()
schedule.run_all(x=new_x, y=new_y)

docs.title: Shared Parameters
docs.text:
When parameters are shared, only specify the parent path:

# If model has sharing: line_2.amplitude -> line_1.amplitude
# Only specify the parent path

schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[(100, 0.1)],
    params={
        "line_1.amplitude": sp.free_in(0),  # Parent path
        # "line_2.amplitude": ...           # Don't specify - it's shared!
    },
)

# Check available paths if unsure:
print(model.get_parameter_paths(show_shared=False))  # Parent paths only
print(model.get_parameter_paths(show_shared=True))   # All paths

docs.title: Full Example: Spectral Line Fitting
docs.text:
import spectracles as sp
import jax.numpy as jnp
import jax.random as jr

# Build a spectral-spatial model
model = sp.build_model(
    MySpectralModel,
    n_spatial=64,
    n_spectral=100,
)

def loss_fn(model, data):
    pred = model(data)
    return jnp.mean((pred - data.flux) ** 2)

# Three-phase optimization strategy
schedule = sp.build_schedule(
    model, loss_fn,
    phases=[
        (500, 0.05),   # Phase 0: Establish spatial structure
        (200, 0.01),   # Phase 1: Refine line parameters
        (100, 0.001),  # Phase 2: Polish everything
    ],
    params={
        # Spatial coefficients: always free
        "spatial.*.coefficients": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),

        # GP kernel: freeze initially, then optimize
        "spatial.*.kernel.*": sp.free_after(1),

        # Line amplitudes: reinitialize at phase 1
        "lines.*.amplitude": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2) | sp.init_normal(1, std=0.1),

        # Line positions: fix until final polish
        "lines.*.center": sp.free_in(2),

        # Line widths: optimize from phase 1
        "lines.*.width": sp.free_after(1) | sp.init_value(1, 1.0),

        # Continuum: always free
        "continuum.*": sp.free_in(0, 1, 2),
    },
    key=jr.key(0),
)

# Run optimization
schedule.run_all(data=my_data)

# Get result
final_model = schedule.model_history[-1]
